A1.justification: Both are complete 18-page versions of the same work. Their text, equations, Table 1, Figures 1–7 and Appendices A–B support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original antibody-optimisation and viral-escape simulations, computational timings, and sequence and binding-pose analyses, including appendix results.

after.justification: v7 retains these original simulation, timing and data-analysis results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The zero-sum payoff, viral mutation-selection process, Monte Carlo antibody optimisation and pruned Absolut!/JAX binding computation remain unchanged. Sections 4.2–4.3 reorder and reindex descriptions of the same updates.

E1.justification: Both use dengue envelope antigen 2R29 and the same antibody-design and simulated viral-escape scenarios, including the appendices. References to other pathogens and cancer do not represent additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Both compare shapers with myopic antibodies and compare the JAX implementation with original Absolut! in Table 1. Newly cited coevolution and forecasting works are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Both retain the usual 30 optimisation steps, horizons 0/5/10/20/100, 100-step evaluation, population sizes 15 and 40, and fixed-binding-budget comparison. Low-resolution training and high-resolution verification also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The horizon/budget comparisons, cross-antibody evaluation, amino-acid distributions and binding-pose analyses are retained in Figures 2–5. Appendices A–B retain the same viral-mutation distribution and full pose-matrix grid in Figures 6–7.

E5.justification: Figure 2 retains standard-error reporting, and the simulation-averaging descriptions and five Monte Carlo roll-outs remain unchanged. No new seed information, repeated-run disclosures, confidence intervals or statistical tests appear.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains timings of 1.8 seconds for Absolut! and 2.1 x 10^-4 seconds for Absolut! + JAX. Figures 2–7 retain the same plotted results and findings, including the shaping advantage, computational trade-off and sequence/pose patterns.

T1.justification: The payoff, expected trajectory fitness, pose-space and binding-energy definitions are unchanged. Equation renumbering and equivalent reindexing of evolutionary updates introduce no new mathematical assumptions, results or proofs.

C1.justification: Both present a simulation proof of concept for antibodies that anticipate and influence viral escape, outperform myopic designs over longer horizons, and potentially inform future therapies. The rewritten abstract, introduction and discussion retain these contributions and their scope.

C2.justification: v7 adds reduced GPU data movement as a tentative explanation for the pruning speedup in Section 4.4 and more explicitly interprets HIV antibody cooperation as analogous to shaping in Section 3. The principal shaping/robustness trade-off and biological-model limitations remain.

D1.justification: v1 describes the implementation and input sources without explicit code or binding-pose data access instructions. v7 adds Sections 5–6 providing access information for the implementation, reported-result code and binding-pose data, plus an abstract code link. This substantially expands reproducibility access information; the linked resources themselves are not verified by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v7 adds Janssen et al. and Zaman et al. on coevolution and Han et al. on antigenic-evolution prediction, modestly broadening the discussion's context. The central positioning around opponent shaping and Absolut! remains; the updated M-FOS publication entry represents the same work.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially condensed and reorganised, with accompanying abstract revisions and rewritten optimisation and cross-evaluation explanations. Sections 4.2–4.3 present the loops more directly, discussion paragraphs are reorganised, and availability sections are added. Together these constitute extensive editorial restructuring.

P2.justification: All seven figures and the timing table retain their graphical content. Figure 5 moves earlier, surrounding text and tables reflow, and several captions receive limited clarifications. No new visual result display is introduced.

improvement.justification: v7 adds explicit code and pose-data access information and clarifies the introduction and evolutionary update descriptions, improving reproducibility documentation and readability. The empirical evidence and main biological-model limitations remain unchanged. The new unresolved citation in Section 5 is a small presentation defect that does not outweigh these limited gains.
